title: Rockets @ Spurs — James Harden's made dunk not counted; Rockets protest denied, 135-133 2OT final stands (Dec 3-9, 2019)
incident_summary: With 7:50 left in the fourth quarter and Houston leading 102-89, James Harden stole the ball and dunked it with such force that the ball cleared the net, whipped around the rim and bounced upward/out — creating the appearance of a miss. The officiating crew did not count the basket and ruled the ball out of bounds off Harden; the Rockets' attempt to challenge the call was not granted. Houston argued the made basket was worth two points and the score was recorded incorrectly (a misapplication of rules, not a judgment call). The Rockets filed a formal protest within the 48-hour window seeking to replay the final 7:50 from that point. On Dec 9, 2019, Commissioner Adam Silver denied the protest; the league disciplined the three officials for misapplying the Coach's Challenge rule and acknowledged that a properly granted replay would have shown the basket counted. The 135-133 double-overtime Spurs win stands and the two points were never added.
scoring_play: James Harden (HOU) steal and dunk — physically a made basket (league later acknowledged replay would show it counted), ruled no-basket on the floor.

originally_reported.basis: On-floor ruling Dec 3, 2019 (crew chief James Capers postgame explanation; protest reporting via USA Today, NBC Sports).

corrected_value.basis: No correction was ever applied — the basket was never added to the score. The league acknowledged the error but denied the protest.

final_official.basis: Final official result; protest denied Dec 9, 2019 (CNBC, Click2Houston/AP).

sources_disagreed: On-floor officials' ruling (no basket) vs. video evidence and the league's own post-hoc acknowledgment (basket was good)
Rockets' position (misapplication of rules: made basket must score) vs. Spurs' position (no misapplication; Rockets had 2OTs to win) — Silver sided with Spurs that a protest replay was not warranted
Crew chief's postgame account (basket-interference reviewable; challenge not made within 30 seconds) vs. Rockets' account (no basket-interference call was made; D'Antoni not granted a challenge)

cause.detail: Two confirmed elements: (1) officials misjudged a made dunk as a miss in real time because of the ball's unusual ricochet; (2) the crew misapplied the Coach's Challenge rule by failing to grant Houston's challenge — the league disciplined all three officials (James Capers, Kevin Scott, John Butler) for this. Whether D'Antoni requested the challenge in time remains disputed between the crew and the team.
